plans.name: WHO healthy diet
plans.summary: Limits on fat, saturated fat and sodium; at least 25 g of fibre and 3,510 mg of potassium a day.

sources.title: Healthy diet, fact sheet of 26 January 2026
Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIV: the energy in a gram of fat, protein and carbohydrate, used here to turn grams into a share of energy

checks.label: Fat, share of energy
checks.basis: WHO: total fat 30% or less of total daily energy

checks.label: Saturated fat, share of energy
checks.basis: WHO: no more than 10% of total energy from saturated fat

checks.label: Carbohydrate, share of energy
checks.basis: WHO: approximately 45–75% of total daily energy

checks.label: Protein, share of energy
checks.basis: WHO: 10–15% of total daily energy is generally sufficient for adults

checks.label: Fibre
checks.basis: WHO: at least 25 g of naturally occurring dietary fibre a day

checks.label: Sodium
checks.basis: WHO: less than 5 g of salt a day (2 g of sodium)

checks.label: Potassium
checks.basis: WHO: at least 3,510 mg a day may be beneficial for adults

unmeasured: Free sugars under 10% of energy: the food tables give total sugars, and cannot tell free sugars from the rest.
At least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day: the food tables do not say which foods are fruit or vegetables.
No more than 1% of energy from trans fat: the food list carries no trans fat value.

plans.name: Two fasting days a week
plans.summary: Two days a week on up to a quarter of your energy need. Defined by an international consensus; recommended by no public body found.

sources.title: International consensus on fasting terminology. Cell Metabolism 2024;36(8):1779–94 — “modified fasting”: “limiting energy intake to typically up to 25% of energy needs on modified fasting days”, for example “on 2 separate or consecutive days per week”

sources.by: Henry CJK; European Food Safety Authority
sources.title: The energy need the quarter is taken of: Henry’s equation times EFSA’s activity level

checks.label: Fasting days this week
checks.basis: A day counts when what you logged comes to a quarter of your energy need or less (Koppold et al. 2024)

unmeasured: A day you logged nothing on is not counted as a fasting day: formicaria cannot tell fasting from not writing it down.
plans.caution: This is a definition, not advice. The consensus says therapeutic fasting is individually tailored and medically supervised fasting is led by a trained physician.

plans.name: Alternate-day modified fasting
plans.summary: A day of eating freely, then a day on up to a quarter of your energy need. A definition, not a recommendation.

sources.title: International consensus on fasting terminology. Cell Metabolism 2024;36(8):1779–94 — alternate-day modified fasting: “alternating a day of eating ad libitum and a day of modified fasting”

sources.by: Henry CJK; European Food Safety Authority
sources.title: The energy need the quarter is taken of

checks.label: Fasting days this week
checks.basis: Every other day is three or four days of a week; a day counts at a quarter of your energy need or less

unmeasured: That the days alternate: formicaria counts them and does not check their order.
A day you logged nothing on is not counted as a fasting day.
plans.caution: This is a definition, not advice. The consensus says therapeutic fasting is individually tailored and medically supervised fasting is led by a trained physician.

plans.name: Time-restricted eating
plans.summary: All eating inside a part of the day, leaving at least 14 hours without. Measured from the times of what you log.

sources.title: International consensus on fasting terminology. Cell Metabolism 2024;36(8):1779–94 — “a daily fasting window of at least 14 hours. There is no explicit limit on energy intake during eating hours”

checks.label: Hours without eating, overnight
checks.basis: Koppold et al. 2024: a daily fasting window of at least 14 hours. Measured from the last thing with energy you logged the day before to the first that day

checks.label: Days you kept to it this week
checks.basis: You say so each day, if you would rather not rely on the times

unmeasured: Anything eaten and not logged, or logged later without correcting its time: an entry's time is when you logged it unless you change it.
Three of the consensus's experts would have preferred a window of at least 12 hours; the number is yours to change.
plans.caution: This is a definition, not advice.

plans.name: Norwegian 4×4 intervals
plans.summary: Four 4-minute efforts hard enough that you cannot speak in sentences, with 3 easy minutes between, two or three times a week. From a research group in Trondheim.

sources.title: Advice on exercise: “We … recommend 4x4-minutes interval training to improve fitness”; 2–3 sessions a week to increase fitness, one to maintain it
Aerobic high-intensity intervals improve VO2max more than moderate training. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2007 — 40 moderately trained men, 8 weeks
Generation 100, BMJ 2020 — 1,567 people aged 70–77 for 5 years: “All cause mortality did not differ between the control group and combined MICT and HIIT group”

checks.label: 4×4 sessions this week
checks.basis: CERG: “we recommend 2–3 sessions with interval training per week” to increase fitness; one a week maintains it

describes: Warm up for 10 minutes at an easy effort
4 minutes hard: 85–95% of your maximum heart rate — by feel, breathing so hard you cannot speak in sentences, yet able to do another interval afterwards
3 minutes of easy movement (about 70% of maximum heart rate), not standing still
Do that four times in all, then cool down for 5 minutes
New to it: start with one 4-minute effort and add one as the weeks go (CERG's 7-week programme)
No heart-rate monitor is needed (CERG). Log each session as the activity “4×4 intervals”
unmeasured: Whether each effort reached the intensity: formicaria counts the sessions you log, not your heart rate.

Its originator says “there are no studies that show that 4×4 interval training prolongs life more than any other type of exercise” (Wisløff, 2024). It is one well-studied way to raise fitness, not a better one than all others.
plans.caution: CERG: “We have positive experience with 4x4 interval training for people with coronary artery disease. However, every patient is different, and if you're unsure you should contact your doctor.”

examples.title: 7 week fitness program — Week 1
examples.note: Week 1 of the 7-week programme by the Trondheim group that devised the 4×4: it starts with one 4-minute effort and builds to four by week 4; a starting point only — CERG itself says to take an extra week or two if the pace is too hard.

examples.meets: named_days "4×4 intervals" (min 2): Mon + Fri = 2 — but only if the build-up sessions are logged under that name: Monday is 1 × 4 minutes and Friday 2 × 4, not four. The first full 4×4 is Monday of week 4; weeks 4, 6 hold two full 4×4 sessions, week 7 one. Session lengths: Mon 10+4+5 = 19 min; Fri 10+4+3+4+5 = 26 min; Wed 10+20 = 30 min.
examples.later: Transcribed from the page (PDF agrees). Full 4×4 = 10 warm-up, 4 hard / 3 relaxed walking ×4 (last one followed by the cool-down), 5 cool-down = 40 min; 3×4 = 33 min; 2×4 = 26; 1×4 = 19. WEEK 2 — Mon: 1×4 kick-start. Wed: 3×4 interval. Fri: core strength, after a 10-minute warm-up: split-squat, squat jumps, push-ups, 5–10 repetitions each, 30 seconds rest between exercises, 1 minute between each of 3 series. Weekend: favourite activity for more than 60 minutes. WEEK 3 — Mon: 3×4. Wed: an activity you do not normally do, more than 60 minutes. Fri: 1×4 kick-start. Weekend off. WEEK 4 — Mon: 4×4 Health Booster. Wed: 4×4 again. Fri: 1×4 kick-start, then core strength: squats 10, split-squat 7 each foot, squat jumps 5, push-ups as many as you can; then squats 7, split-squat 5 each foot, squat jumps 5, push-ups as many as you can. Weekend off, or low-to-moderate only. WEEK 5 — Mon: 1×4 kick-start. Wed: 20-minute Fun-Run (after 10 warm-up), then core strength: 10 push-ups, 15 squats, 10 squats with jumps, three series (30 s between exercises, 1 min between series). Fri: an unfamiliar activity, more than 60 minutes. WEEK 6 — Mon: 4×4. Tue: 20-minute Fun-Run + core strength (10 push-ups, 15 squats, 10 squat jumps, once). Thu: 4×4. Fri: 20-minute Fun-Run + core strength (10 push-ups, 15 squats, 10 squat jumps, three times). WEEK 7 — Mon: 4×4. Wed: an unfamiliar activity, more than 60 minutes. Thu: as many sit-ups as you can, a 30-minute walk or jog at a conversational pace, as many sit-ups as you can. Sessions a week: 3 in weeks 1, 3, 4, 5, 7; 3 plus a weekend activity in week 2; 4 in week 6. Interval sessions a week (any length): 2, 2, 2, 3, 1, 2, 1.

plans.name: Activity for losing weight
plans.summary: More than 250 minutes of moderate activity a week, with strengthening on 2 days to keep muscle. Written for people above a healthy weight, and it works with eating less, not instead of it.

sources.title: Donnelly et al. 2009, position stand: “Moderate-intensity PA between 150 and 250 min wk(-1) will provide only modest weight loss. Greater amounts of PA (>250 min wk(-1)) have been associated with clinically significant weight loss.”

sources.by: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
sources.title: Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition (2018): “Muscle-strengthening activities can also help maintain lean body mass during weight loss.”

checks.label: Activity this week
checks.basis: ACSM 2009: more than 250 min a week of moderate activity for clinically significant weight loss; 150–250 gives only modest loss. A vigorous minute counts as two.

checks.label: Strengthening days this week
checks.basis: WHO and the US guidelines: all major muscle groups on 2 or more days a week; it helps keep lean mass while weight is lost

describes: Diet and activity together: “Combining both caloric restriction and physical activity tend to be most beneficial for weight loss” (US guidelines)
Strength training adds little weight loss of its own; it is there to keep muscle (ACSM 2009)
Intervals and steady effort lose the same fat when the energy spent is the same; intervals take less time (reviews of trials)
No body defines “toning” or “definition”, and exercising one area does not take fat from that area: a review of 37 comparisons found “no spot reduction”
unmeasured: What you eat: follow a diet under Food for that.
A rate of loss. Every figure a public body gives (about 0.5 to 1 kg a week) is addressed to people above a healthy weight; none was found for someone already at one.
plans.caution: CDC: “if you have a chronic health condition, be sure to talk with your doctor about the types and amounts of physical activity that are right for you.” A healthy weight for adults is generally a body mass index between 18.5 and 24.9 (NHLBI); this is not for losing weight below it.
